messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — opened a docs PR with a canary toggle example for Dedicated provisioning. Want a fast sanity check before I merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842 :eyes:

devin: link works, reading now. main questions: where does this live in the nav, and do we need a terraform example too?

maria: plan is to put it under /docs/dedicated/provisioning/canary-rollouts. I added a short Terraform snippet and a minimal CLI dry-run. Terraform snippet (inline):
```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "canary" {
  name = "tenant-canary"
  gpu_type = "a100-80gb"
  reserved_capacity = 2
  preemptible = false
}
```

liam: wording nit — we currently use both "preemption" and "eviction" across docs. For dedicated customers we should standardize to "eviction" + brief parenthetical about preemption where needed. Docs PR should update the SLA language too.

maria: good catch. I changed the example text to say "eviction (preemption for best-effort workloads)" — can someone from product + legal sign off on that phrasing?

zoe: From platform side: can we add a short autoscale policy sample and a recommended dry-run checklist? Suggest adding this command to the checklist: `rwctl capacity apply --dry-run --tenant tenant-canary` and a note to check the Dedicated Console for pending allocations.

maria: adding that. Proposed autoscale snippet (JSON) — can we validate quickly that fields match runtime schema?
```json
{
  "scalePolicy": "cpu-based",
  "minReplicas": 1,
  "maxReplicas": 4,
  "targetCPUPercent": 65
}
```

devin: looks fine but rename `scalePolicy` -> `policyType` to match the SDK. Also add `gracePeriodSeconds` for canary ramp. I'll push a tiny commit.

rachel: legal quick note — anywhere we say "data never leaves region X" we need the usual caveat about backups and logs. In this example page please add one line: "Customers should verify backup targets and logging endpoints to meet residency requirements."

maria: thanks, adding that sentence under "Data residency and isolation". Also adding a one-liner about SLA impact for canary pools: "Canary pool capacity is best-effort; production SLAs only apply to committed reserved pools." Li am / rachel can you confirm?

liam: confirmed from product side. Maybe add a callout box explaining fallback behaviour when canary capacity isn't available.

maria: added callout and an example failover policy snippet: `fallback_model: "small-medium"` and a note to route critical traffic to reserved pools.

devin: pushed the `policyType` + `gracePeriodSeconds` change and a tiny phrasing tweak. CI is running.

deploy-bot: ci/circleci — build #842 passed :white_check_mark:

maria: awesome, thanks all. I'll merge after one more :thumbsup: from docs or platform. If no objections, I'll cherry-pick a small note into the migration guide for tenants moving reserved -> canary first.

zoe: :+1: please include the dry-run checklist steps under "Onboarding checklist" so oncall can follow the same flow.

maria: will do, merging in ~30m unless anyone needs a block. Thanks! :party:
